label: Bible Study
prompt: Whoso findeth a _____ findeth a good thing, and obtaineth favour of the LORD.
verse: Whoso findeth a wife findeth a good thing, and obtaineth favour of the LORD.
note: A short, sweet proverb about marriage — finding a wife is finding a good thing.

label: Warm-Up Word
prompt: Be strong and courageous, be not afraid nor dismayed for the king of Assyria, nor for all the multitude that is with him: for there be _____ with us than with him:
verse: Be strong and courageous, be not afraid nor dismayed for the king of Assyria, nor for all the multitude that is with him: for there be more with us than with him:
note: Hezekiah faces Assyria's huge army with a simple headcount: there be more with us than with him.

label: Sunday School
prompt: So David took the spear and the _____ of water from Saul's bolster; and they gat them away, and no man saw it, nor knew it, neither awaked: for they were all asleep; because a deep sleep from the LORD was fallen upon them.
verse: So David took the spear and the cruse of water from Saul's bolster; and they gat them away, and no man saw it, nor knew it, neither awaked: for they were all asleep; because a deep sleep from the LORD was fallen upon them.
note: David crept into Saul's camp and left with the king's spear and water cruse — proof he could have struck, and didn't.

label: Deep Water
prompt: And they continued stedfastly in the apostles' doctrine and _____, and in breaking of bread, and in prayers.
verse: And they continued stedfastly in the apostles' doctrine and fellowship, and in breaking of bread, and in prayers.
note: The first church's four habits after Pentecost: teaching, fellowship, bread and prayer — still a decent checklist.

label: Don't Play With Me
prompt: All things are lawful for me, but all things are not _____: all things are lawful for me, but all things edify not.
verse: All things are lawful for me, but all things are not expedient: all things are lawful for me, but all things edify not.
note: 'All things are lawful… but not expedient' — Paul's two-part test: is it allowed, and is it actually helpful?
